error.signature: AI treats South Africa as malaria-free or omits malaria risk for a Kruger/Mpumalanga/Limpopo itinerary

verdict.summary: South Africa is not uniformly malaria-free: the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) designates the low-lying parts of Limpopo and Mpumalanga (including Kruger National Park) and far northern KwaZulu-Natal as malaria-transmission areas, with risk highest in the rainy season, while Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Durban itself carry no malaria risk.

dead_ends.action: Skip antimalarial prophylaxis for a Kruger/Mpumalanga/Limpopo safari because 'South Africa' as a whole is treated as malaria-free
dead_ends.why_fails: NICD's national guidelines and Kruger-specific advisory identify the Kruger National Park, the Mpumalanga and Limpopo lowveld, and far northern KwaZulu-Natal as active malaria-transmission areas; the risk is real even though major cities like Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Durban have none, so a trip combining a city stay with a Kruger safari still carries risk on the safari leg.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers generalize from a Cape Town or Johannesburg city itinerary (no malaria risk) to the whole country, missing that the risk is geographically concentrated in the lowveld/Kruger region and highly seasonal.

workarounds.action: Take antimalarial chemoprophylaxis for overnight stays in Kruger, Limpopo, or Mpumalanga lowveld camps, and use mosquito-bite prevention year-round
workarounds.how: NICD's national malaria prevention guidelines list doxycycline and atovaquone-proguanil as chemoprophylaxis options (doxycycline added as a pharmacist-dispensable Schedule 2 medicine in January 2024); risk is highest September/October to May. Combine with DEET repellent, long sleeves after dusk, and sleeping under nets or in screened/air-conditioned rooms.

workarounds.action: Seek urgent medical testing for any fever or flu-like symptoms within weeks of leaving a malaria area
workarounds.how: NICD advises that anyone with fever or flu-like symptoms after visiting a risk area must get an urgent blood test, since severe malaria can develop within days if diagnosis is delayed.
